parsed.explanation: The combined regime imposes universal traveller-facing exposure: passports/visas cannot show affirmed markers, visa officers must refuse where documents cast doubt on sex, and a possible lifetime fraud ineligibility follows alleged misrepresentation — travellers have been stranded. Federal orders bar trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities, with state bans layered on top (four states criminalising in circumstances). Detention chains are documented as harmful: birth-sex ward placement, a conversion-therapy-style federal corrections policy, and immigration-custody abuse (beatings, solitary, sexual violence). This division bans under-18 care and adult surgery has contracted. Offsetting: no identity criminalisation, no sodomy law, a federal hate-crime statute, and courts that have enjoined multiple orders with live litigation. Social opinion is majority-restrictive.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 order ended X markers and requires assigned-sex-only passport/visa markers; cable directs refusal where discrepancy casts 'reasonable doubt' on sex, with case-note tagging and consideration of permanent lifetime fraud ineligibility; travellers report passports blocked/confiscated, leaving some stranded abroad. Universal-exposure document regime.
entry_documents.protection: Pre-existing X passports valid to expiry; fraud finding requires all four elements, is never automatic, and has limited waivers; civil-liberties suit pending; legal-aid FAQ on document rules maintained.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate to investigation → immigration detention → birth-sex placement and custody abuse documented elsewhere in the dossier.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau adopted a state model mandating conversion-therapy-style treatment of trans inmates (hair cut short, hormones removed, psychiatric substitution); immigration custody reports from trans men include forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse; a trans woman was held 24 hours in a men's ward after a restroom arrest.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Federal gender-identity hate-crime statute; courts have blocked or enjoined several January 2025 orders; legal-aid and consular channels exist.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border document discrepancy → refusal/investigation → detention places the traveller inside the birth-sex custody regime, where federal hostile policy operates with functioning enforcement.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities nationwide; 21+ state/provinces ban identity-congruent facility use (9+1 covering all government buildings), 6 extend to private settings, and 4 make use a criminal offence in certain circumstances.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 state/provinces, 4 units and the capital have no mapped ban; the trespass offence requires willful entry plus refusal to depart, not automatic arrest.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal order sets the floor, state bans add criminal exposure; this division's own ban status is not identified in the dossier.

care_services.exposure: Division statute (in force 1 July 2023) bars under-18 hormone therapy/surgery with licence revocation; a coastal hospital cancelled all gender-affirming surgeries on 13 Feb 2025 including an adult's pre-approved procedure; national funding restrictions and proposed under-18 insurance bar apply.
care_services.protection: Public-employee health plan settlement obliges payment for medically necessary care, possibly out-of-state for minors; HRT started before 1 July 2023 grandfathered; litigation pending.
care_services.interaction: An adult visitor seeking routine or transition-related care risks refusal following national funding directives; a travelling trans minor has no lawful in-division transition care, and any willing out-of-state provider interacts with the licence ban.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises neutralising groups 'radically pro-transgender'; DOJ memo lists 'radical gender ideology' among violent-extremist viewpoints; official language calls youth care 'mutilation'; 66% back sex-at-birth document rules and 69% athlete bans; advocates describe genocide-stage parallels.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Memo states the reward is not conditioned on gender ideology and counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; employment non-discrimination ruling and marriage equality remain in force.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile official framing raises severity of any police or border encounter, even while street-level police locally called anti-trans violence 'epidemic-level' and investigated it.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division statutory ban on under-18 transition care with licence revocation; federal order on schools and 'gender ideology'; national proposed public-insurance bar for under-18s; facility bans reach K-12 in 19+ state/provinces.
minors_guardians.protection: Grandfathering for minors already on HRT; the employee plan settlement can fund minors' care obtained outside the division; challenges pending.
minors_guardians.interaction: An adult travelling with a trans minor cannot obtain transition care in the division; providers face penalties, and any incident interacts with federal facilities and document rules.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: City police documented three violent crimes against trans women in 2023 (two fatal shootings a week apart) and described violence against Black/Brown trans women as epidemic-level; the 4.8/100k killing figure is an acknowledged undercount floor with no denominator and is not usable as a magnitude.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police publicly investigated and characterised the violence; federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 23 state/provinces cover gender identity in bias-crime statutes.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence rate versus background is not established, so severity rests on documented incidents plus the responsiveness of police and courts rather than a measured campaign.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Litigation unresolved across passport, executive-order and health rules; measures shift with court rulings; this division's facility-ban status, hospital-suspension permanence and per-capita violence data are undocumented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have blocked or enjoined several orders; civil-liberties suit active; legal-aid FAQ maintained; federal hate-crime statute; 22 state/provinces plus the capital bar gender-identity discrimination.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Functioning courts mitigate where they grant relief, but a standing order efficiently enforced remains exposure; uncertainty about which measures are in force raises discovery risk at travel time.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: Vellandra's register produces consistent exclusion with appeals that never succeed; here the visa/passport regime also yields routine refusal and stranded travellers. Lower than 0.35-A because there is no standing entry register — refusal depends on document discrepancy, the fraud finding is never automatic with waivers available, litigation is live, and courts have enjoined sibling orders. Sits a step above that anchor's exclusion-only ceiling.

Higher than this case: Kestrel Isles offers only discretionary secondary screening and administrative refusal with written reasons, appeal and consular notice, no custody-harm chain. This dossier adds documented immigration-custody abuse, a federal conversion-therapy corrections policy, criminal facility exposure in four states, care bans and majority-restrictive opinion, so it must sit materially below 0.55-B.

Materially higher than this case: Meridia has trained respectful border staff, brief detention, counsel access and compensation for unlawful holding. Here federal policy mandates assigned-sex markers, directs refusal on doubt and threatens lifetime ineligibility, with custody abuse documented — no comparable respectful-inspection or remedy regime. Far below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The two layers compound rather than cancel. Federal document rules create a universal border exposure for any trans traveller whose papers invite doubt, with refusal, case-note tagging and a possible lifetime fraud bar — and the dossier's own chain shows discrepancy escalating into detention, where birth-sex placement, a conversion-therapy-style corrections policy and documented immigration-custody abuse operate through efficient institutions (hostile policy plus functioning enforcement is exposure, not recourse). Federal facility exclusion plus state bans adds a second universal-exposure layer; this division adds an under-18 care ban and contracted adult surgery. Mitigation is real but partial: no identity criminalisation, a federal hate-crime statute, active litigation and courts that have enjoined several orders, and police who investigated local anti-trans killings. Public opinion is majority-restrictive, and the violence rate versus background is not established, so violence weights below the state-imposed exposures.
